classification.difficultyReason: Reuse the joint probability from part (a), find the complementary Sunday branch and add the two disjoint ways to watch on Monday.

content.prompt: Michael found that in general, the probability that he watched TV on Sunday was $0.3$. If he watched TV on Sunday, then the probability that he watched TV on Monday was $0.6$. If he did not watch TV on Sunday, then the probability that he watched on Monday was $0.55$. For a given week, find the probability that he watches TV

answer.worked:
Let $S$ be watching TV on Sunday and $M$ be watching TV on Monday.

$$\begin{align*}P(S\cap M)&=P(S)P(M\mid S)\\P(S\cap M)&=0.3\times0.6\\P(S\cap M)&=\frac{9}{50}\end{align*}$$

Let $S$ be watching TV on Sunday and $M$ be watching TV on Monday. Part (a) gives $P(S\cap M)=0.18$.

$$\begin{align*}P(\bar S)&=1-0.3=0.7\\P(\bar S\cap M)&=P(\bar S)P(M\mid\bar S)\\P(\bar S\cap M)&=0.7\times0.55=0.385\\P(M)&=P(S\cap M)+P(\bar S\cap M)\\P(M)&=0.18+0.385\\P(M)&=\frac{113}{200}\end{align*}$$
